title: A tool ledger for a 20-person team
scenario:
Harbor Lane Events is a 20-person event agency. Your colleague drafted the team's tool ledger: which tools, helpers, apps and agents the team uses, who owns each, and what each costs per month. You check it before the director signs it.

Use the exhibit. The agency, people, plans and the ChatGPT price are made up for this case. The Claude seat price is Anthropic's US list price. Product facts are from the vendors' help pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
BRIEF (made up):
  Harbor Lane Events, 20 people. Ledger for Q4.
  Main assistant: Claude, Team plan.
  Sales also has a ChatGPT Enterprise workspace.

TOOLS:
  Claude Team     20 seats   owner: Dana (ops)
  ChatGPT Ent.     6 seats   owner: Dana (ops)

HELPERS:
  "Venue quote" (custom GPT, sales)
    instructions + 3 price files + a custom action
    that reads live prices from the booking system.
    Plan: migrate it to a plugin on Friday, then
    switch the GPT off.            owner: Leo (sales)

APPS:
  Google Drive connector (Claude)
    Plan: attach it to the public "Client briefs"
    project so all 20 can search client folders.
                                   owner: Dana (ops)

AGENTS:
  "Deposit chaser" (Claude Cowork, scheduled)
    Every night: read the shared events inbox and
    email each new client a deposit request.
    Mode: Skip all approvals.      owner: Ines (finance)

OWNERS:
  "Supplier rates" (Claude project, private)
    Only member: Mara. Mara leaves on 31 October.

BUDGET (shown per month):
  Claude Team   annual plan, renews 1 March
                20 Standard seats x $20   = $400
                (US list price, annual, Oct 2026)
  ChatGPT Ent.   6 seats x $60 (made up)  = $360
  Note: "Two people left in September. We removed
  them, so from October the Claude seats cost
  18 x $20 = $360 a month."

questions.prompt: HELPERS: what must Leo plan for before the GPT is switched off?

options.text: Nothing; the move carries over every part of the GPT unchanged
options.explanation: OpenAI lists parts that do not carry over, such as custom actions and the selected model.

options.text: Uploading the three price files again, which the move leaves out
options.explanation: OpenAI says migration brings over the GPT's knowledge files and connected apps.

options.text: Rebuilding the booking-system action, which the move leaves out
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI: migration turns instructions into a skill and brings over files and apps, but custom actions must be rebuilt separately.

options.text: Nothing, as long as he picks the same model the GPT used before
options.explanation: OpenAI says the selected model does not carry over, and custom actions must still be rebuilt.

questions.prompt: APPS: why will the Drive plan not work as written?

options.text: On Team plans, connectors work only inside private projects
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic, for Team and Enterprise plans: connectors are only available in private projects.

options.text: Drive connectors need an Enterprise plan, not a Team plan
options.explanation: Anthropic describes Owners enabling connectors on both Team and Enterprise plans.

options.text: A project can use only one person's Drive account at a time
options.explanation: No page says that. Each person signs in to their own account; the problem is the public project.

options.text: Public projects can't search files, only answer from chats
options.explanation: No page says that. Anthropic's rule is about where connectors are available: private projects only.

questions.prompt: AGENTS: what is the right change to the deposit chaser?

options.text: Run it locally, so client emails never leave Ines's laptop
options.explanation: Local does not mean the data stays on the laptop. And the risk is the sending, not where it runs.

options.text: Keep it as is, since the cloud task is isolated from harm
options.explanation: Anthropic: isolation limits where code runs, not what Claude reads or does.

options.text: Switch to Automatically approve, so it uses less of the plan
options.explanation: Anthropic says auto mode uses more of your usage limit than the other modes.

options.text: Have it draft the requests for review, not send them alone
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: don't schedule tasks that send messages on your behalf. It also reads an inbox anyone can write to.

questions.prompt: OWNERS: what must happen before Mara leaves?

options.text: Nothing; an Owner gets her projects when she is removed
options.explanation: That is OpenAI's rule for ChatGPT. On Claude, other members can't open a removed member's private project.

options.text: Mara gives a teammate Can edit on the project before removal
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: private projects close to others when their member is removed, so she must invite someone with Can edit first.

options.text: Mara shares one chat from the project with the whole team
options.explanation: Anthropic says chats a removed member shared stop working after removal. Share the project, not a chat.

options.text: Mara turns off project sharing, so the project stays put
options.explanation: Turning sharing off blocks new shares. It does not hand the project to anyone.

questions.prompt: BUDGET: is the note about the Claude seats right?

options.text: Yes, removing them refunds their seats from October onward
options.explanation: Anthropic: removing members does not trigger an immediate credit or refund.

options.text: Yes, but only if the two people never used usage credits
options.explanation: Usage credits are a separate line. Removing members does not cut the seat bill either way.

options.text: No, the seats stay paid until the count is cut at renewal
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: removal frees the seat but gives no refund. Reduce the total seat count; that takes effect at the next renewal.

options.text: No, a Team plan can never lower its total number of seats
options.explanation: Anthropic says owners can reduce the seat allocation. It takes effect at the next renewal.
